unit.unitTitle: Who Is This? People and Family

cefr.bandName: Pre-A1, from no English at all

unit.unitOverview:
Name the people around you.
Say who they are to you.
Use he and she, not just the name.
Point and say: this is my sister.
unit.learningPath:
Listen to the lesson.
Words: people and family.
Patterns: this and that, he and she.
Listen to three short texts.
Say who is in your family.
Write three lines about a person.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
functions: Name a person: man, woman, boy, girl
Say who a person is to you
Use he and she instead of a name
Point out a person near you and further away
Say how many people are in your family
unit.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending

visual.lectureScript:
This is Unit 5. Today, people.
Until now you talked about yourself.
Now you talk about other people.
First, four words. Listen.
A man. A woman. A boy. A girl.
A man is big. A boy is young.
A woman is big. A girl is young.
Say them with me. Man. Woman. Boy. Girl.
Now your family.
Mother. Father. Sister. Brother.
Say them with me.
And two more. Wife. Husband.
Now, a small word that saves you.
You do not say the name every time.
For a man or a boy, say he.
For a woman or a girl, say she.
Listen. This is Ben. He is my brother.
This is Ana. She is my sister.
Say it with me. He is. She is.
Last, pointing.
Near you: this is my friend.
Far from you: that is my teacher.
This for near. That for far.
And the question: Who is this?
That is Unit 5. Go and talk about people.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: He and she
grammar.explanation:
You do not say the name every time.
One small word does it.
He for a man or boy. She for a woman or girl.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
Ben is my brother.  →  He is my brother.
Ana is my sister.   →  She is my sister.

man, boy, father, brother, husband, son  →  he
woman, girl, mother, sister, wife, daughter  →  she
grammar.workedExample:
You want to talk about Ana.
1. Say her name once: This is Ana.
2. Now do not say it again.
3. Ana is a woman, so use she.
4. Say: She is my sister.
5. Say: She is a nurse.
grammar.commonMistake:
Many languages use one word for both.
English has two, and they are not the same.
Using he for a woman is a real mistake here.
grammar.memoryTip: He for a man. She for a woman.
grammar.practice:
He or she?
1. My father. ___
2. My sister. ___
3. The boy. ___
4. The woman. ___
5. My husband. ___
6. The girl. ___
grammar.answerKey:
1. He
2. She
3. He
4. She
5. He
6. She
Five or six right? Good. This one matters.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: This and that
grammar.explanation:
Both point at a person or a thing.
The difference is how far away it is.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
Near you:        This is my friend.
Further away:    That is my teacher.

This is my bag.   (in your hand)
That is my bag.   (across the room)
grammar.workedExample:
Your sister is beside you.
1. She is near, so use this.
2. Say: This is my sister.
3. Your teacher is across the room.
4. Far, so use that.
5. Say: That is my teacher.
grammar.commonMistake:
Do not use this for everything.
English speakers hear the difference.
Near is this. Far is that.
grammar.memoryTip: This for near. That for far.
grammar.practice:
This or that?
1. The book in your hand. ___
2. The man at the door. ___
3. Your friend beside you. ___
4. A car in the street. ___
5. The pen you are holding. ___
grammar.answerKey:
1. This
2. That
3. This
4. That
5. This
Four or five right? You can point in English.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: Who is this?
grammar.explanation:
One question for a person.
The answer gives a name, or says who they are.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
Who is this?
This is Ana.
She is my sister.

Who is that man?
That is my father.

who = a person
what = a thing
grammar.workedExample:
A person points at your friend.
1. They ask: Who is this?
2. Give the name: This is Ana.
3. Then say who she is to you.
4. Say: She is my friend.
5. Two short lines is a good answer.
grammar.commonMistake:
Do not use what for a person.
No: What is this? (about a person)
Yes: Who is this?
grammar.memoryTip: Who is for people. What is for things.
grammar.practice:
Who or what?
1. ___ is this? It is a pen.
2. ___ is this? This is my sister.
3. ___ is that man?
4. ___ is in your bag?
grammar.answerKey:
1. What
2. Who
3. Who
4. What
All four? You can ask about people and things.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: One or more than one
grammar.explanation:
Most words add s for more than one.
Three words here do not.
Learn those three now.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
one friend  →  two friends
one sister  →  two sisters

But:
one man    →  two men
one woman   →  two women
one child   →  two children

people is already more than one
grammar.workedExample:
You have two of them.
1. The word is sister.
2. Is it one of the three strange ones? No.
3. So add s.
4. Say: two sisters.
5. Now try man. It is strange: two men.
grammar.commonMistake:
Do not say two mans or two childs.
These three change their shape.
And never say one people. Say one person.
grammar.practice:
Write the plural.
1. one brother, two ___
2. one man, two ___
3. one child, two ___
4. one friend, two ___
5. one woman, two ___
grammar.answerKey:
1. brothers
2. men
3. children
4. friends
5. women
Four or five right? Good. The three strange ones are common words.

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — Man, woman, boy, girl
speaking.instructionsAndModelLines:
Tap Listen. You will hear about a person.
Say: man, woman, boy or girl.
1. He is forty. He is my father.
2. She is eight. She is my sister.
3. She is thirty. She is my teacher.
4. He is ten. He is my son.
5. He is fifty. He is my uncle.
6. She is six. She is my daughter.
Tap the mic. Say six answers.

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — Who is in your family?
speaking.instructionsAndModelLines:
Say four lines about your family.
1. My family is (big or small).
2. My mother is (something about her).
3. My father is (something about him).
4. We are (a number) people.

Tap again. Listen back.

speaking.aiTutorPrompt: Tell the tutor about two people in your family. Ask it a question back.

4. A: What does he do? B: He is a driver.

1. my father
2. my sister
3. the boy

speaking.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
speaking.title: Speaking 6 — The th in this and that
speaking.instructionsAndModelLines:
Listen and repeat.
this ... that ... the ... they
Put your tongue between your teeth.
Let the air come out.
It is not d. It is not z.
Now say these lines.
This is my mother.
That is my brother.
Tap the mic. Say both lines.
Check: can you feel your tongue between your teeth?
speaking.aiTutorPrompt: Ask the tutor to say this and that. Say them back.

writing.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
writing.title: Writing 1 — Three people
writing.promptAndInstructions:
Write three lines.
One line for each person in your family.
Use he or she in each line.
writing.modelText:
My mother is a teacher. She works at a school.
My father is a driver. He works at night.
My sister is a nurse. She is twenty.
writing.successCriteria:
Three lines.
He or she in each one.
Each line starts with a capital.
Each line ends with a full stop.
writing.support: Write one line only. Add the others later.
writing.extension: Add a line about a friend.

writing.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
writing.title: Writing 2 — One person, three things
writing.promptAndInstructions:
Choose one person you know.
Write three short lines about them.
Say who they are. Say what they do.
writing.modelText:
This is Ana.
She is my friend.
She is a nurse and she is kind.
writing.successCriteria:
Three lines about one person.
You name them in the first line.
You use he or she after that.
Each line has a full stop.
writing.extension: Now write three lines about a second person.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
teacherNotes.noteType: He and she is a real mistake, not a small one
teacherNotes.note: Many languages use one pronoun for both, so a learner may call their mother he for months without noticing. English listeners hear it immediately and it can sound careless when it is nothing of the kind. Correct it every time, kindly, and say why.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
